title: Chiral fermions on the lattice: the fermion doubling problem
bottleneck: Discretizing spacetime for lattice field theory generically produces spurious 'doubler' fermion species, and defining a single chiral fermion, as the weak interaction requires, on the lattice took decades and remains technically intricate. A fully satisfactory non-perturbative definition of chiral gauge theories is still incomplete.
why_it_blocks: The Standard Model is a chiral gauge theory; without a rigorous lattice definition, non-perturbative questions about the electroweak sector, including baryon-number violation, cannot be settled from first principles.
current_state: Ginsparg-Wilson fermions and domain-wall formulations provide workable chiral symmetry on the lattice and are used in production simulations, but a complete construction of chiral gauge theories remains open. The overlap operator satisfies an exact lattice chiral symmetry, but extending it to fully chiral gauge theories with anomalies remains incomplete.
